newsitem.title: USA: House votes to override Clinton veto of abortion bill.
newsitem.headline: House votes to override Clinton veto of abortion bill.

text.p: The House Thursday voted to override President Clinton's veto of a bill to ban so-called "partial birth" abortions, sending it to the Senate where backers appear short of the two-thirds majority needed to follow suit.

The House voted 285-137 to override, narrowly garnering the needed vote. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott has said he will schedule a Senate vote next week, even while admitting bill supporters are unlikely to prevail in that chamber.

While Congress appeared unlikely to override the veto, the House action and expected Senate vote will likely accomplish what supporters of the legislation hope for -- once again focusing voters' attention on the highly emotional issue.

Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole has attacked Clinton for vetoing the bill, promising conservative groups to sign it if elected. The Catholic church has mounted an aggressive effort in support of the measure.
Clinton said he has concerns about the abortion procedure, but could not sign the bill because it did not contain constitutionally required protections for a woman's health.

The legislation, vetoed by Clinton in April, marks the first time Congress has voted to ban a specific abortion procedure since the Supreme Court's landmark 1973 Roe vs. Wade deicsion making abortion legal.
